Events.title: Load the data
Events.detail: Run your libname program and import the raw tables for this domain. Make sure DM is mapped first: every domain takes USUBJID and the study day reference from it.

Events.title: Inspect the raw data
Events.detail: Look at one subject end to end, list the distinct values of coded fields, and note partial or oddly formatted dates.

Events.title: Identifiers
Events.detail: STUDYID, DOMAIN and USUBJID. Build USUBJID with exactly the same rule as in DM.

Events.title: Event term and coding
Events.detail: --TERM as collected, then the dictionary-coded --DECOD and hierarchy (MedDRA for AE and MH).

Events.title: Qualifiers
Events.detail: Category, severity, seriousness, outcome, relationship and similar collected details, recoded to controlled terminology.

Events.title: Timing
Events.detail: Dates in ISO 8601, then study days from DM.RFSTDTC, EPOCH and visit variables.

Events.title: Sequence number
Events.detail: Sort by USUBJID and the domain's natural keys, then number the records within each subject.

Events.title: Order, labels and lengths
Events.detail: Keep only this domain's variables in SDTMIG order with the standard labels. Move extra collected data to SUPP--.

Events.title: Run the P21-lite checks
Events.detail: Run them with --dm pointing at your DM so subjects and study days are checked too.

Events.title: Export to XPT
Events.detail: Write a version 5 transport file named after the domain, e.g. ae.xpt.

STUDYID.tip: The same constant study identifier as in DM.

DOMAIN.tip: The two-letter domain code as a constant.

USUBJID.tip: Must match DM.USUBJID exactly: build it with the same rule, never re-derive it differently.

--SEQ.tip: A number unique for each record within USUBJID in this domain. Derive it last, after sorting, so it is stable.

--GRPID.tip: Groups related records within a subject, e.g. the records of one panel. Optional.

--SPID.tip: Sponsor-defined identifier, often the CRF line or page number. Useful for tracing back to the CRF.

--REFID.tip: Internal or external reference, e.g. a lab accession number.

--TERM.tip: The verbatim term exactly as collected (spelling errors included). Upper-casing is acceptable; do not recode it.

--MODIFY.tip: The term after the coder changed the verbatim text to code it. Only when it differs from --TERM.

--DECOD.tip: The dictionary-derived term (MedDRA preferred term for AE and MH, WHODrug for CM) or controlled terminology value.

--LLT.tip: MedDRA lowest level term from your coding output.

--HLGTCD.tip: MedDRA high level group term code.

--BODSYS.tip: Body system or organ class used for analysis; for MedDRA-coded events this is the primary SOC.

--SOCCD.tip: MedDRA primary system organ class code.

--CAT.tip: A grouping you define, e.g. the CRF page the data came from. Use consistent upper-case values.

--SCAT.tip: A sub-grouping within --CAT. Only use it together with --CAT.

--PRESP.tip: "Y" when the event or treatment was pre-printed on the CRF (asked about specifically). Empty for spontaneously reported items.

--OCCUR.tip: "Y" or "N" for pre-specified items only, answering whether it occurred. Leave empty for spontaneously reported items.

--STAT.tip: "NOT DONE" when a pre-specified item or test was not done or not asked. Leave results empty on those records.

--REASND.tip: Why the item was not done. Only filled when --STAT is "NOT DONE".

--TRT.tip: The treatment name exactly as collected (CM) or the protocol-defined treatment name (EX).

--DOSE.tip: Numeric dose per administration. If the dose was collected as text or a range, use --DOSTXT instead.

--DOSTXT.tip: Dose as text, for non-numeric values like "200-400" or "<1".

--DOSU.tip: Units for --DOSE, from the UNIT codelist, e.g. "mg".

--DOSFRM.tip: Dose form from the FRM codelist, e.g. "TABLET".

--DOSFRQ.tip: Dosing frequency from the FREQ codelist, e.g. "QD" or "BID".

--ROUTE.tip: Route from the ROUTE codelist, e.g. "ORAL".

--INDC.tip: The condition the treatment was given for, as collected.

--CLAS.tip: Drug class from the dictionary, e.g. the ATC class used for analysis.

--LOC.tip: Anatomical location from the LOC codelist, e.g. "ARM".

--LAT.tip: Side from the LAT codelist: "LEFT", "RIGHT" or "BILATERAL".

--POS.tip: Body position during the test from the POSITION codelist, e.g. "SITTING".

--SEV.tip: Severity from the AESEV-style codelist, e.g. "MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE".

--TESTCD.tip: Short test code from controlled terminology. At most 8 characters, starting with a letter, only letters, digits and underscores.

--TEST.tip: Test name matching --TESTCD from the same codelist. At most 40 characters.

--SPEC.tip: Specimen type from the SPECTYPE codelist, e.g. "SERUM" or "URINE".

--METHOD.tip: Method of the test, e.g. "DIPSTICK", from the METHOD codelist.

--FAST.tip: "Y" or "N": was the subject fasting? Only when collected.

--ORRES.tip: The result exactly as collected or received, as text.

--ORRESU.tip: Units of --ORRES from the UNIT codelist (match case, e.g. "mmHg", "kg").

--ORNRLO.tip: Lower end of the normal range, in original units, as text.

--ORNRHI.tip: Upper end of the normal range, in original units, as text.

--STRESC.tip: The result in a standard format and units, as text. Every non-empty --ORRES needs one.

--STRESN.tip: Numeric copy of --STRESC when --STRESC is a number; empty otherwise.

--STRESU.tip: Standard units for --STRESC and --STRESN, the same for every record of a test.

--STNRLO.tip: Lower end of the normal range in standard units (numeric).

--STNRHI.tip: Upper end of the normal range in standard units (numeric).

--NRIND.tip: Where the result falls against the normal range, e.g. "LOW", "NORMAL", "HIGH" (NRIND codelist).

--LOBXFL.tip: "Y" on the last non-missing result before first exposure to study treatment, per subject and test; empty otherwise. This replaces --BLFL as the main baseline flag in SDTMIG 3.4.

--BLFL.tip: Baseline flag. In SDTMIG 3.4, prefer --LOBXFL; use --BLFL only if your sponsor still needs it.

--DRVFL.tip: "Y" when the record was derived rather than collected (e.g. a calculated average).

--TOX.tip: Toxicity description, e.g. the CTCAE term.

--TOXGR.tip: Toxicity grade, e.g. "1" to "5" for CTCAE.

--CLSIG.tip: "Y" or "N": clinically significant, as judged by the investigator.

VISITNUM.tip: Numeric visit number matching TV.VISITNUM for planned visits. Unplanned visits get a number between the visits around them, e.g. 3.01.

VISIT.tip: Visit name matching TV.VISIT for planned visits, e.g. "WEEK 4"; for unplanned visits use something like "UNSCHEDULED 3.01".

VISITDY.tip: Planned study day of the visit, from TV.

TAETORD.tip: Order of the element within the subject's arm, from TA. Derive by comparing the record date with SE.

EPOCH.tip: The trial epoch the record falls in (e.g. "SCREENING", "TREATMENT", "FOLLOW-UP"), derived from the subject's elements in SE.

--STDTC.tip: Start date/time in ISO 8601. Keep partial dates partial; never impute in SDTM.

--ENDTC.tip: End date/time in ISO 8601. Leave it empty for ongoing records and use --ENRTPT and --ENTPT instead.

--DY.tip: Study day of --DTC relative to DM.RFSTDTC: date minus RFSTDTC plus 1 on or after RFSTDTC, date minus RFSTDTC before it. No day 0. Only when the date is complete.

--STDY.tip: Study day of --STDTC relative to DM.RFSTDTC: date minus RFSTDTC plus 1 on or after RFSTDTC, date minus RFSTDTC before it. No day 0. Only when the start date is complete.

--ENDY.tip: Study day of --ENDTC, calculated the same way as --STDY. No day 0.

--DUR.tip: Duration in ISO 8601 (e.g. "P3D"), only when collected, not derived from start and end.

--TPT.tip: Planned time point name, e.g. "PRE-DOSE" or "2H POST-DOSE".

--ELTM.tip: Planned elapsed time from the reference point, in ISO 8601 duration, e.g. "PT2H".

--RFTDTC.tip: Date/time of the reference point named in --TPTREF.

--ENRF.tip: End relative to the study reference period: "BEFORE", "DURING", "AFTER", "DURING/AFTER", "U". Use when only that was collected.

--ENRTPT.tip: End relative to a reference time point, e.g. "ONGOING" when the item continues at the time named in --ENTPT.

--ENTPT.tip: The reference time point for --ENRTPT, e.g. "END OF STUDY".

--STRTPT.tip: Start relative to a reference time point, e.g. "BEFORE".

--NAM.tip: Name of the laboratory or vendor that did the test.

general_tips.iso8601: Dates in SDTM are character values in ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss with a time. Keep partial dates partial ("2023-05" or "2023"), never impute them in SDTM. In SAS, the E8601DA. and E8601DT. formats write these from SAS date and datetime values.
general_tips.codelist: Values must match the CDISC submission values in the codelist exactly, including case.
general_tips.suppqual: Collected data with no standard variable in the domain go in a SUPP-- dataset (e.g. SUPPAE), not as extra columns.
